notes: Family arm: rules benefit 0.000; LinUCB minus rules per seed 0.000, 0.000, 0.000; hard-rule violations 0/0/0/0 -> criterion UNTESTABLE: no arm asked a single question on the validation families (questions asked per arm: 0/0/0/0), so benefit is 0 for every selector by construction and this says nothing about LinUCB versus rules. Simulator arm (not the shipping criterion): LinUCB minus rules per seed 0.100, 0.140, 0.080 -> above rules by >= 0.05 on all seeds.

The simulator benefit depends on the visible features by construction (firsthand knowledge, decisive gaps): the LinUCB advantage there shows only that the contextual model can learn them (policies/README.md).
LinUCB is deterministic: the 3 family-arm seeds only change the order of the training families. Variation across seeds is therefore small by design and is not a stochastic confidence interval.
Training data is tiny (7/7/7 labelled questions per seed); unanswered questions are skipped, never scored 0.

Family arm asked 0 questions on validation for every selector (0/6 investigations): the frozen family-arm criterion could not be evaluated. The plan words E03 as "on the simulator"; that arm passes the >= 0.05 on all 3 seeds bar with 0 ineligible selections, but it is simulated and favours learnable visible features by construction.

Rules benefit is bounded by the baseline pipeline: most recommendations stay "none" with the default extraction, so few questions can change a recommendation toward the expected class (see E00 notes).
